# Declarative checks — review

Status: review record for #838, following up #827 (declarations moved to
`packs/<pack>/declared-checks.json`). Covers five questions: the vocabulary's generality, message
discipline, what else converts, engine performance, and what the linter field teaches. The engine
under review is [engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs](../../engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs);
its design record is [engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md). All numbers measured
2026-08-14 on this checkout (610 tracked files, Node 22).

## The short version

- **The architecture is validated by the field.** ESLint, Vale, Spectral and markdownlint all
  converged on the same shapes this engine already has: rules as data over a shared single-pass
  scan, per-rule severity in repo config, findings that carry their own teaching text. Nothing
  surveyed is adoptable as a dependency under the vendored-verbatim / zero-dependency constraints —
  the win is importing idioms, and several of the best are already here (Vale's document-part
  scoping ≈ `checkSections`; Spectral's `given`/`then` ≈ the parsed-doc assertions).
- **Generality**: 10 of the 18 spec keys are single-use — the per-case reading is right for the
  long tail. Three key clusters are the same idea spelled thrice and can merge; four cross-rule
  facilities (named file classes, structural self-exclusion, a rule-level `fix` default,
  comment-blind scanning) would remove most of the boilerplate that makes declarations long.
- **Messages**: the median message field is 16 words but the tail runs to 58; fix strings restate
  whole policies and repeat verbatim within rules. The field's discipline — quote the evidence,
  state one action — plus a meta-check over the spec files themselves (the format is JSON, so the
  meta-lint is a schema plus word caps, itself landable as a declared check) closes it.
- **Conversion**: 5 of 61 imperative code rules convert today with zero vocabulary change (the five
  jwt rules — one shared mechanism, ~220 lines to delete); ~5 more with three genuinely general
  key additions. The other ~50 stay imperative for structural reasons (git state, session
  transcript, config-driven scans, real parsing, cross-file joins). The bigger cleanup there is
  helper consolidation: four copies of comment-stripping, three hand-rolled config-schema
  validators, three base-vs-head JSON key diffs.
- **Performance**: the whole-repo world sweep is 0.67s; the declarative engine is already the fast
  path (all 25 declared rules share one ~35ms scan). The two real boosts are the `barrier` rule
  (274ms — 61% of rule time, re-extracting per-line candidates once per edge) and the base-ref
  refresh fetch (0.7–8s of network per run, paid again on every Stop-hook turn with changes).

## 1. The measured state

89 registered rules across canon + local packs: 25 pattern-declared (JSON), 3 barrier edges
declared as pack-manifest data (a second, older declarative vocabulary), 61 imperative code rules.
All 13 work-scoped rules are imperative — `patternRule` has no work-scope vocabulary (nothing over
added lines, commits, or the transcript), so every declared check is world-scoped by construction.

Key usage across the 25 declarations: `matchLines` 6, `checkEachFile` 5, `checkSections` 5,
`relevantWhen` 5 — the workhorses — then a long tail of one use each: `maxLines`,
`coveredByGlobLine`, `listedInFile`, `checkKeyValueFile`, `equalParsedValues`, `requirePaths`,
`whenMissing`, `checkParsedFile`, `forEachParsedEntry`, `repoWide`, `skipLinesMatching`.

Whole-repo world sweep (35 active world rules on the home): 0.67s wall without the base-ref fetch,
1.43s with it. Phase split: module imports 22ms, pack discovery 44ms, context build 42ms, rules
452ms. Slowest rules: `barrier` 274ms, `pack-discovery-entry-await` 55ms, the entire declared-rule
family ~35ms (billed to whichever declared rule runs first — the shared-scan design working as
intended), `warning-suppression` 24ms, `markdown-link-labels` 12ms.

## 2. Generality (task 1)

The per-case shape is real but concentrated: the workhorse keys are genuinely general, and the
long tail is one key per converted check. Three clusters are the same idea under different names
and can collapse without inventing a query language:

| Cluster | Keys today | One idea |
|---|---|---|
| Bounds | `maxLines`; `minBullets`/`maxBullets`/`maxBulletBlockLength` (inside `checkSections`) | a count/length bound over a unit (lines, bullets, characters) |
| Index coverage | `listedInFile`, `coveredByGlobLine` | every selected path must be covered by an entry in an index file — the two differ only in what an entry is (an `asText` template vs a first-token glob) |
| Parsed-document assertions | `checkParsedFile`, `forEachParsedEntry`, `equalParsedValues` | select nodes by field path (with filters), then assert — Spectral's `given`/`then`, already backed by one shared parse cache and `fieldAt` |

The parsed-document merge is the highest-value one: a `checkParsedFiles` entry with a field-path
selector (`inFilesMatching`/`file` + `atField` + `whereFieldEquals`) and a small closed assertion
set (`requireField`, `forbidField`, `forbidValueInArray`, `equalsFieldIn` another file) carries all
three current keys plus the next several structured checks, and message placeholders (`{path}`,
`{value}`) fall out of the selector. Spectral's `@key` addressing (assert on key names, not
values) is the one missing capability the current `fieldAt` model can't express.

Two consolidations are cheaper than they look and remove more authoring friction than any key
merge — the boilerplate is what actually makes declarations read as verbose:

- **Named file classes.** `excludeFiles` regexes for test files are hand-repeated
  (`google-token-email-verified`, `web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide` carry near-identical
  test/fixture exclusions), and every skill's checks hand-exclude the skill's own directory
  (`"excludeFiles": "/^skills\\/google-id-token-validation\\//"`). Named classes usable at
  `scanFiles`/`excludeFiles` (`"testFiles"`, `"codeFiles"`, `"workflowFiles"`) mirror Vale's
  scopes and ESLint's shared settings; the self-exclusion shouldn't even be a class — the engine
  knows which directory a declaration file lives in, so excluding the declaring skill's own tree is
  structural (the canon's own prefer-structural-classifier rule, applied to the engine).
- **Rule-level message defaults.** `in-session-github-access` repeats one 30-word `fix` three
  times; `product-wiki-growth-log` repeats its fix three times. A rule-level `fix` (and `what`)
  default inherited by assertions, overridable per assertion, removes the duplication the
  format's no-comments rule otherwise amplifies.

And one capability gap: the imperative side has string-aware comment stripping
([engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs](../../engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs)); the
declarative side only has `skipLinesMatching`, which `in-session-github-access` uses as a weaker
approximation (`/^\s*(\/\/|\*|\/\*)/` misses trailing comments and can match inside strings). A
`scanIgnoringComments: true` key backed by `stripComments` (newline-preserving, so line numbers
hold) makes the declarative form as precise as the code it replaces — and is a precondition for
converting most code-facing candidates.

What NOT to do: a general selector algebra (JSONPath, ast-grep's `all`/`any`/`not`/`inside`
composition) as the base vocabulary. The corpus's own rulings decide this — keys must read alone
to a cold reader (#789/#799), and a knob nobody would set differently shouldn't exist (#707). The
composition vocabulary is the growth path *when a real check needs it*, added as wordy named keys,
not a platform to build ahead of need. Single-use keys whose semantics are genuinely distinct
(`checkKeyValueFile`, `repoWide`) are fine as they are: each is data over shared machinery, and
deleting them buys nothing.

## 3. Message discipline (task 2)

A declared check's failure renders `what` + `failureMessage` (as the why line) + `fix`. Median
field is 16 words; the tail: `web-speech-capture-released-on-pagehide.fix` 58 words,
`google-token-email-verified.failureMessage` 47, `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor.fix` 44,
`product-wiki-freshness.fix` 40 (with an embedded JSON snippet). The long ones share a shape:
`failureMessage` argues the rule's philosophy in multiple clauses, and `fix` restates the whole
policy including its alternatives instead of naming the one action.

The surveyed tools converge on a tight message discipline (ESLint's ecosystem enforces
`^[A-Z].*\.$` — a complete sentence stating the problem; Semgrep interpolates the matched text into
the message; Vale caps a message at what the writer must do):

- **`what` quotes the evidence.** State the violated expectation with the matched content in it —
  the engine's `{match}`/`{path}`/capture-group interpolation exists; use it everywhere. A finding
  that quotes the offending token is actionable; one that restates the rule is not.
- **`fix` is one imperative clause** — the single next action. Alternatives, escape hatches, and
  policy context are the `failureMessage`'s one causal clause or nothing. When a fix wants a menu,
  that's usually the rule doing two jobs (or prose that belongs in the pack's README).
- **`failureMessage` is the consequence, once** — why the defect bites, ≤ ~20 words. Where `what`
  already implies it, shorter still. (It doubles as the catalog description in `--list`, which
  rewards the one-line form.)
- **Enforce it with a meta-check.** The format being JSON makes this cheap and is the field's
  "lint the linter" idiom (`eslint-plugin-eslint-plugin`): a declared check over
  `packs/*/declared-checks.json` — word caps per field, no fix string repeated verbatim within a
  rule (that's the rule-level default's job), interpolation keys that exist. The existing
  vocabulary can carry the word caps today; the rest is a small imperative check or a schema.

Fixture discipline transfers too: ESLint's RuleTester contract — every rule tested as
(input text, expected findings) pairs through the real engine, every message exercised — is the
see-it-fail rule in executable form, and
[engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs](../../engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs) already runs that
way. Worth pinning as the convention when the meta-check lands: a declared check with no fixture
exercising it is a finding.

## 4. What else converts (task 3)

Full per-rule audit: 61 imperative code rules (plus one CLI-only gate and the 3 barrier-data
edges). Verdicts:

**Convertible now, zero vocabulary change — 5 rules, one cluster.** The five jwt rules
(`jwt-hardcoded-secret`, `jwt-sign-sets-expiry`, `jwt-none-not-accepted`,
`jwt-verify-binds-audience`, `jwt-verify-pins-algorithms`) are all the same mechanism: select
non-test source files → gate on the file importing the library → optionally bail on a word
appearing anywhere in the file → flag lines matching a call pattern. That is exactly
`scanFiles` + `excludeFiles` + `whenFileMatches` + `unlessFileMatches` + `matchLines`. Converting
them deletes ~220 lines plus the pack's `scan.mjs` and is the single best next conversion.
(Partial conversions also available now: `product-wiki-layout`'s `requirePaths` half,
`skill-no-enforcement-narration`'s runner-mention half.)

**Convertible with a small, genuinely general extension — ~5 rules.** Ranked by the #707 test
(who else would use the key):

| Extension | Carries | General? |
|---|---|---|
| `unlessPreviousLineMatches` on a matchLines assertion | `warning-suppression` (reason-above-the-marker) | yes — previous-line context is a standard line-scan concept |
| `maxLineLength` (bytes) beside `maxLines` | `rules-line-length` | yes — every prose-width rule |
| `andLineMatches` (second must-also-match pattern) | `task-phase-discipline` | yes — conjunction on one line |
| whole-text multiline match (`matchText`) | `sudden-termination-vs-teardown` | borderline — one user today |
| match-count / numeric-capture range | `scheduler-workflow-shape`'s cron legs | borderline — Vale's `occurrence` says the count form recurs; the numeric range is one user |

A key added for exactly one rule reproduces the per-case smell — the borderline two should wait
for a second customer.

**Stays imperative — ~50 rules**, for causes the vocabulary shouldn't chase: git history/diff/base
state (14 — all work-scoped rules among them), session transcript (3), project/pack config driving
the scan (9), pack metadata via `ctx.packs` (5), real parsing — balanced brackets, indentation
state, HTML attributes, TOML (16), cross-file joins where one file's parsed value names the other
(8). A declarative work scope (assertions over added lines) would cover only ~3 rules today — not
worth the vocabulary until that changes.

**The cheaper wins in the imperative corpus are consolidations, not conversions:**

- Four separate comment-stripping implementations (`code-scanning.mjs`'s, leaflet's
  length-preserving fork, and two local-pack copies) → one helper with a `preserveOffsets` option.
- Three hand-rolled pack-entry config validators (`growth-config`, `preferences-store-configured`,
  `barrier`'s config half) → one declarative config-schema seam on the pack manifest (ESLint's
  `meta.schema` idiom).
- Three base-vs-head JSON key diffs (`node/earn-each-dependency`, `cer/permission-added-store-issue`,
  `adoption-answers-pending`) → a `work.addedKeys(file, atPath)` helper.
- The near-identical `cer/release-workflows` / `sw/release-workflows` pair → shared
  "vendored set present" machinery, with the `requirePaths` halves declarable today.

1. **The `barrier` scan re-derives per-line candidates once per edge** (274ms, 61% of rule time).
   the barrier engine (at review time `packs/barriers/engine.mjs`; since moved to
   [engine/checks/helpers/reference-scanning.mjs](../../engine/checks/helpers/reference-scanning.mjs))
   runs `candidatesOn(line)` (two
   regex sweeps) and `resolveRef` per candidate inside `scanEdge`, so a `siblings` edge — expanded
   to one sub-edge per child directory — and any overlapping edges recompute identical extraction.

   neither `.` nor `/`) stacks on top. Expected: most of the 274ms on multi-edge repos.
2. **The base-ref refresh fetch is the dominant wall-clock item** (~0.75s here, up to its 8s
   timeout; `refreshBaseRef` in
   [engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs](../../engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs)) — and
   the Stop hook pays it on every turn with tracked changes. The fetch exists for work-scope
   honesty (the stale-base false-verdict class DESIGN.md documents) and must stay; the boost is a
   freshness window —
   skip the fetch when the remote-tracking ref was already refreshed within the last few minutes

   entirely in world-`all` runs is tempting but wrong to do blind: `--changed` scoping and the
   delta context still derive from the merge-base.)

Not worth taking: the per-file `existsSync`+`statSync` pair and the ~10 git spawns in context
build (42ms total), and pack discovery's eager imports (44ms — load-bearing for structural
discovery, #581).

## 6. Technology review (task 5)

Constraints that frame every verdict: plain Node ≥18, zero dependencies, the engine vendored
verbatim into members, everything must run on credentials and settings members already have. A
tool members must install is dead-on-arrival per the standing ruling (a missing binary = the
capability silently dead per repo); a native-binary npm dependency breaks vendored-verbatim.

### The tools

| Tool | What it is | Verdict for us |
|---|---|---|
| **ESLint v10** | JS linter; since v9.7 a language-agnostic core with official JSON/Markdown/CSS language plugins — rules are `{meta, create}` listeners over a shared parse | Not adoptable (JS-ecosystem dependency tree), but the strongest source of idioms: `meta.messages` with `{{placeholders}}`, `meta.schema` validating per-rule options, capability flags (`fixable`, `hasSuggestions`), RuleTester's valid/invalid contract, and meta-linting rules themselves. Its `no-restricted-syntax` — a generic engine rule instanced by per-config selector+message data — is the field's endorsement of exactly the `patternRule` design (and its findings all reporting one shared rule id is the weakness our per-spec `id` already avoids) |
| **ast-grep** | Rust/tree-sitter structural search; YAML rules (`pattern`/`kind`/`regex` atoms, `inside`/`has` relations, `all`/`any`/`not` composition); Node via `@ast-grep/napi` | **Poor fit.** Our targets are Markdown prose, YAML workflows, JSON configs — Markdown isn't a built-in language (custom grammar = per-platform native artifact), plain text isn't a language at all, and napi is a 0.x native addon resolving nine platform-specific binaries. For config files, path-shaped queries (Spectral) beat CST compositions. Steal the rule-file vocabulary (`id/message/severity/note/fix`, named `utils` sub-rules, the composition algebra) as a future growth path, not the tool |
| **Semgrep** | OCaml/Python semantic grep; `patterns`/`pattern-either`/`pattern-not-inside`, metavariables interpolated into messages; `generic` mode for config-ish text | Non-embeddable (no Node surface; CLI install per member) and the official rules are under an internal-use-only license. Steal: AND/OR/not-inside vocabulary, metavariable-in-message, `focus-metavariable` (match wide, report narrow), per-rule `paths.include/exclude` |
| **remark-lint / markdownlint / textlint** | Markdown/prose linters over mdast / micromark tokens / TxtAST | The dependency trees don't transfer; the contracts do. markdownlint hands every rule both the token stream *and* raw `lines` — endorsement of our line-first engine with an optional structural layer (which `checkSections` already is). Its `fixInfo` (`{lineNumber, editColumn, deleteCount, insertText}` — a fix as a data splice) is the most vendorable autofix model surveyed, the natural shape if declared checks ever grow fixes. Container suppression (ignore matches inside code fences) should be engine-default — `markdownIndex` already blanks fences for sections; line rules don't get that for free yet |
| **Vale** | Go prose linter: styles = directories of YAML rules, each `extends` one of 11 closed primitives (`existence`, `occurrence`, `substitution`, …), with `scope:` targeting document parts (heading/paragraph/list/code) | The closest architectural cousin, independently converged: closed primitive set instantiated by data ≈ the assertion vocabulary; `scope` ≈ `checkSections`. Its `occurrence` primitive (min/max matches in scope) confirms the bounds-cluster merge in §2; single-binary Go distribution confirms there's no free lunch for prose linting as a dependency |
| **Spectral** | Node JSON/YAML linter: `given` (JSONPath) selects nodes, `then` (`field` + function from a small closed set: `pattern`, `truthy`, `defined`, `schema`, `enumeration`, `length`) asserts; `{{path}}`/`{{value}}` message placeholders; `@key` addresses key names | ~20 runtime dependencies — not adoptable. The `given`/`then` decomposition is the model for the parsed-document merge in §2, implementable as a dot-path subset over the existing `fieldAt` + [minimal-yaml](../../engine/checks/helpers/minimal-yaml.mjs) machinery (the YAML half the field solves with heavy parsers, this engine already solved with a vendored minimal one) |
| **actionlint / yamllint** | Deep GitHub-workflow checker (typed `${{ }}` expression checking against modeled contexts) / YAML style checker | actionlint's depth comes from modeling the platform's types — beyond our economics to build, wrong to imitate with regexes. The defensible integration is additive-when-present: a member CI step, or invoked only if the binary exists with an explicit "tool absent, skipped" note (never silent). yamllint: closed rule set, notable only as severity/inline-disable prior art |

### Cross-cutting idioms worth importing

Beyond the ones already folded into §§2–3 (message discipline, meta-lint, named scopes, rule-level
defaults, fixture contract):

- **Dual-tier remediation** — auto-applied `fix` vs human-opted `suggestion`, declared as a
  capability in rule metadata. Relevant only if declared checks grow fixes; if they do,
  markdownlint's data-splice shape keeps the spec pure JSON.
- **Rule tags** for bulk toggling (markdownlint's `headings`/`whitespace`; Semgrep categories).
  At 89 rules with per-pack activation already doing most of that job, not yet earned.
- **`off` as a severity value** — already exists (`rules: {"<id>": "off"}`); the field confirms
  one-knob-per-rule over separate disable mechanisms.
- **Inline disables** (the five-verb `disable`/`enable`/`disable-line`/`disable-next-line`/
  configure-file grammar, with required reasons). The config-side `accept` mechanism with
  mandatory reasons is deliberately stronger (reviewable in one file, provenance-stamped);
  importing inline disables would weaken it. Noted to reject explicitly.
- **A doc URL riding in the finding** (`meta.docs.url`, Vale `link`): the surveyed tools carry
  one; #827 settled that declarations are self-standing, and the message discipline in §3 is how
  that stays workable.

### Embeddability conclusion

Four options weighed: keep the hand-rolled engine (zero install surface, and the hard parts of the
big tools — JS ASTs, taint analysis, typed workflow contexts — are parts this corpus doesn't
need); depend on `@ast-grep/napi` (native 0.x addon, nine platform binaries — breaks
vendored-verbatim for no Markdown/prose payoff); shell out to member-installed CLIs (violates the
runs-on-what-members-have ruling; Semgrep adds a rules-licensing hazard); or adopt formats without
tools. **The last, on top of the first, wins on every axis** — and is what §§2–5 spell out
concretely.

input.prompt: Describe ast-grep's relational rules: the exact operator names (inside, has, follows, precedes), what each means, and the stopBy/field refinements. Quote key sentences.

List the pattern composition operators Semgrep rules support (patterns, pattern-either, pattern-not, pattern-inside, pattern-not-inside, metavariable-*), what pattern-inside does exactly, and how paths include/exclude work. Quote key sentences.

content.content:
# ast-grep's Relational Rules

ast-grep provides four relational operators that filter target nodes based on their surrounding context:

## The Four Operators

**inside**: "the _target_ node must be **inside** a node that matches the sub rule."

**has**: "the _target_ node must **have** a child node specified by the sub rule."

**follows**: "the _target_ node must **follow** a node specified by the sub rule. (target after surrounding)"

**precedes**: "the _target_ node must **precede** a node specified by the sub rule. (target before surrounding)"

## Key Refinements

### stopBy Parameter
Controls search depth with three options:
- `'neighbor'` (default): matches only direct relationships
- `'end'`: "will make ast-grep search surrounding nodes until it reaches the end"
- Custom rule object: stops searching when the specified rule matches

### field Parameter
Narrows results to specific child relationships. For example, using `field: key` distinguishes between a property key versus its value in object literals.

## Rule Composition

Relational rules accept sub-rules, enabling recursive composition. "All four relational rules accept a sub rule object as their value," allowing complex nested matching patterns using operators like `any`, `all`, and `pattern` within the surrounding node specifications.

const diffBase  = mergeBase || 'HEAD';
const tracked   = lines(gitTry(root,'ls-files'));
const untracked = lines(gitTry(root,'ls-files','--others','--exclude-standard'));
const vsBase    = lines(gitTry(root,'diff','--name-only','--diff-filter=d', diffBase));
let scanned;
if (mode === 'all') scanned = [...tracked, ...untracked];

# Semgrep Pattern Composition and Path Operators

## Pattern Composition Operators

Semgrep supports the following pattern operators for combining multiple patterns:

1. **`patterns`** - "Logical `AND` of multiple patterns," requiring all child patterns to match simultaneously.

2. **`pattern-either`** - "Logical `OR` of multiple patterns," where any single child pattern can produce a match.

3. **`pattern-not`** - "Logical `NOT` - remove findings matching this expression," filtering out unwanted results.

4. **`pattern-inside`** - Keeps matched findings located within specified code structures.

5. **`pattern-not-inside`** - Keeps matched findings that do not reside within specified code structures.

6. **Metavariable operators** including:
   - `metavariable-regex` - Searches metavariables for regex patterns
   - `metavariable-pattern` - Matches metavariables using pattern formulas
   - `metavariable-comparison` - Compares metavariables against Python expressions
   - `metavariable-name` - Constrains identifier types by module origin

## How `pattern-inside` Works

The `pattern-inside` operator functions as a containment filter: "keep matched findings that reside within its expression." It identifies code matching the primary pattern only when that code appears nested inside the specified context pattern.

## Path Include/Exclude Mechanism

Path filtering uses glob patterns relative to the project root. The system operates on two levels:

**Exclusion (highest priority):** "To ignore a specific rule on specific files, set the `paths:` key with one or more filters." These patterns prevent rule execution on matching paths.

**Inclusion:** "To run a rule *only* on specific files, set a `paths:` key with one or more of these filters." When specified, rules apply exclusively to included paths.

Critical note: "When mixing inclusion and exclusion filters, the exclusion ones take precedence."

|---|---|
| `packs/chrome-extension-release/content-script-module-syntax.mjs` | `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/chrome-extension/content-script-module-syntax.mjs` |

---

# 1. `content-script-module-syntax`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/chrome-extension/content-script-module-syntax.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** Two-stage, cross-file. Stage 1: every `ctx.tracked` path matching `/(^|\/)manifest\.json$/` whose raw text contains `"manifest_version"`, `JSON.parse`d; the extension roots are `dirOf(manifestPath)`. Target file set = `manifest.content_scripts[].js[]` run through `resolveFromRoot(root, entry)` (strips a leading `/` or `./`, rejects any entry containing `..`). Stage 2: every `ctx.files` source (`.mjs|cjs|js|jsx|ts|tsx`) whose text contains `registerContentScripts`, from which `registeredScriptPaths()` harvests more targets — each resolved against *every* root and kept only if `ctx.tracked.includes(path)`. Judged set is the `Map<path, declaredIn>`; self-gates to `[]` when no manifest exists.

**Parsing.**
- `stripComments` (shared helper, string-aware state machine).
- `blankLiterals(source)` — hand-rolled quote state machine replacing string/template *contents* with spaces, keeping quotes and newlines so offsets/line numbers are stable.
- `registeredScriptPaths(src)` — a balanced-bracket scan (`depth` over `([{`/`)]}`) from each `\bregisterContentScripts\s*\(` to its matching close, then `/\bjs\s*:\s*\[([^\]]*)\]/` on that argument text, then `/['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g` for literal-only paths.
- `moduleSyntax(text)` — two multiline-anchored regexes over the blanked view: `STATIC_IMPORT = /^[ \t]*import\s+(?:[^\n;()]*?\bfrom\s*)?['"]/m` and `STATIC_EXPORT = /^[ \t]*export\s*(?:\{|\*|default\b|(?:declare\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function|class|type|interface|enum)\b)/m`; earliest of the two wins. This is JS module-level-statement *classification by anchoring*, not an AST — the header's claim is that after blanking, line-start == statement-start for a static import.

**Asserts.** No file named by a content-script `js` array carries a top-level `import`/`export` statement.

**Naive-regex FP.** Header, verbatim: *"grepping every source file for `^import` would flag the whole codebase, because module syntax is correct everywhere except this one injection surface."* Also excluded by construction: dynamic `import(...)` and `import.meta` (the match demands a specifier or binding, never `(`), and module syntax quoted inside a string a script injects elsewhere.

**Minimal declarative capability.** Two pieces, only one of which is pattern-shaped.
- *Non-pattern:* "derive the scanned file set from a parsed field of another file, resolved as a path relative to that file's directory" — a JSON field-path → file-set join. `checkParsedFiles` in `pattern-rules.mjs` can select documents and assert on fields, but cannot turn a field's value into the *scan scope* of a line assertion. This is the genuinely new capability, and it is data-flow, not graph-walk.
- *Pattern:* a `scanIgnoringStringLiterals` source view (sibling to the existing `scanIgnoringComments`) plus ordinary `matchLines`. Fully declarative.
- The `registerContentScripts` half needs balanced-paren + array-literal extraction; it is a secondary target source and could be dropped from a declarative port at the cost of one detection arm.

---

# 2. `declarative-content-set-icon`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/chrome-extension/declarative-content-set-icon.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** `ctx.files` matching `/\.(?:mjs|cjs|js|jsx|ts|tsx)$/` whose raw text contains `declarativeContent` (cheap prefilter). No manifest gate.

**Parsing.** `stripComments` first, then per call site `CALL = /\bdeclarativeContent\s*\.\s*SetIcon\s*\(\s*\{/g`:
- `endOfString(src, i)` — backslash-honoring literal skipper, shared by both passes.
- `objectLiteral(src, open)` — balanced `{[(` / `}])` depth walk from the opening brace, string-aware; returns `null` on an unbalanced (half-written) file, in which case the site is skipped.
- `topLevelKeys(obj)` — a depth-tracking tokenizer that records a key only when a `:` is hit at `depth === 1`, resetting the token at `,` and at every bracket transition; quoted keys (`'path':`) captured via `endOfString`.

**Asserts.** No `declarativeContent.SetIcon({...})` argument object has `path` among its *own* depth-1 keys.

**Naive-regex FP.** Header: *"grep for `path:` would drown in false alarms, and even `SetIcon` alone is ambiguous."* Two named scopings: the `declarativeContent.` qualifier keeps `chrome.action.setIcon({path})` (the *correct* API) quiet, and depth-1-only keeps a `path` nested deeper or in a neighbouring call out of scope.

**Minimal declarative capability.** A **call-argument-object scope**: "for each match of regex X ending at an opening brace, take the balanced brace region and assert over its own top-level key set (`requireKey` / `forbidKey`)". Purely pattern-shaped with a bracket-matching scope primitive; nothing computational. This same primitive covers rule 4.

---

# 3. `leaflet/asset-integrity`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/leaflet/asset-integrity.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** `ctx.files` matching `/\.html?$/i` whose raw text matches `/leaflet/i`.

**Parsing.** `stripHtmlComments` (blanks `<!--...-->` to spaces, newlines kept). Then `TAG = /<(script|link)\b([^>]*)>/gi` per tag, and `attributes(text)` — an attribute tokenizer `/([a-zA-Z_:][-\w:.]*)(?:\s*=\s*("[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^\s"'>]+))?/g` producing a lowercased-name map, valueless attributes mapping to `''`. URL is `attrs.src` for `script`, `attrs.href` for `link`.

**Asserts.** For each tag whose own URL is remote (`/^(?:https?:)?\/\//i`) *and* matches `/leaflet/i`: URL matches `PINNED = /[@/-]\d+\.\d+[\w.+-]*(?:$|[/?#])/`, `integrity` matches `/^sha(?:256|384|512)-\S+/`, and `crossorigin` is present (`!== undefined`). Missing items are joined into one finding.

**Naive-regex FP.** Header: *"grep for `unpkg.com` or `integrity` answers the wrong question. The rule is about one *tag*."* Naively flagged/missed: a locally vendored `js/leaflet.js`, a `<link rel=preconnect>` to the CDN host, a Leaflet URL in page prose, and — the inverse failure — a file where the core bundle *is* hashed so a file-level `integrity` grep passes while a bare plugin tag sits beside it.

**Minimal declarative capability.** An **HTML-tag scope with attribute binding**: "for each `<script|link>` tag, bind its attributes; where `src|href` matches P, require attribute A to match / attribute B to exist". Wholly pattern-shaped, no computation. Note the per-tag *conjunction of attribute assertions producing one message* — the declarative form needs list-valued `missing` interpolation or one finding per missing item.

---

# 4. `leaflet/tile-attribution`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/leaflet/tile-attribution.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** `ctx.files` matching `/\.(html?|mjs|cjs|jsx?|tsx?)$/i` whose text contains `L.tileLayer`. File-level abstain: any file matching `OUT_OF_BAND = /\baddAttribution\s*\(/` is skipped whole.

**Parsing.** The heaviest of the ten.
- `blankComments(source)` — a *length-preserving* clone of `stripComments` (comment chars → spaces). The header states why: *"Offsets have to survive here because the scan reports a line number computed on the blanked text and, for HTML, splices script bodies back at their original positions."*
- `codeView(file, raw)` — for HTML, blanks the entire document to spaces, then splices each `<script>` body (itself comment-blanked) back **at its original offset**, so markup, page text and a Leaflet snippet in a `<pre>` are invisible while line numbers stay true.
- `matchBracket(src, open)` — string/template-aware bracket matcher with a closer stack.
- `splitTopLevel(src, from, to)` — comma split at one nesting level, stepping over nested brackets and literals whole; returns `null` when unbalanced.
- `topLevelKeys(src, open)` — key extraction via `KEY = /^\s*(?:(['"])([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\1|([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*))\s*:/` per member; **returns `null` if any member starts with `...`** (a spread could carry `attribution` in, so absence is no longer provable).

**Asserts.** For each `L.tileLayer(` call: with no second argument → finding; with a second argument that is a brace literal → its own top-level keys must include `attribution`. Anything else (variable, call, spread, unbalanced) → abstain.

**Naive-regex FP.** Header: *"`grep attribution` answers the wrong question — it is satisfied by the word appearing anywhere in the file, and it cannot tell WHICH tileLayer is missing it."* Explicit non-matches: `L.tileLayer.wms(...)` (different constructor), options-by-variable, spread-built options, files using `map.attributionControl.addAttribution(...)`. Half the prose bullet (`maxZoom` = the provider's real ceiling) was judged un-checkable and left as prose.

**Minimal declarative capability.** Same **call-argument-object scope** as rule 2, extended with (a) *argument-index selection* ("the 2nd top-level argument"), (b) an explicit **abstain-when-not-a-literal** semantics, and (c) an existing-style file-level `unlessFileMatches`. The `codeView` HTML-script-splicing is a reusable *source view* ("the JS a page actually runs, offsets preserved") — a view primitive, not computation. Nothing here is graph-shaped.

---

# 5. `signal-teardown-routing`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/macos/signal-teardown-routing.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** All `ctx.files` matching `/\.swift$/`, each read once and `stripComments`ed into a `Map<file, text>`. Double repo gate: some file matches `APPKIT = /\bNSApplicationDelegate\b|\bNSApplicationMain\b|\bNSApp\b/` **and** some file matches `TAP = /\binstallTap\s*\(/`; otherwise `[]`.

**Parsing.** No structural parser — regex sets plus **byte-offset ordering**. `ROUTING` = three alternatives (`makeSignalSource(`, `sigaction(`, `signal(\s*(SIGTERM|SIGINT|SIGHUP)`). Arm 3 uses `text.search(MAKE_SOURCE)` as a start index, sets `RESUME.lastIndex = setup` and takes the first `/\.resume\s*\(\s*\)/` after it, then compares `text.search(SIG_IGN)` against `resumed.index`.

**Asserts.** Three arms: (1) no routing mechanism anywhere → flag at the tap site; (2) routing exists but one of `SIGTERM|SIGINT|SIGHUP` appears in *no* source file; (3) per routing file, `signal(…, SIG_IGN)` must occur at a lower offset than the first `.resume()` following the first `makeSignalSource(`.

**Naive-regex FP.** No `PARSED, NOT GREPPED` banner; the equivalent statement is the gating paragraph — *"Gated twice, so it speaks only where the rule applies… Everything is read with comments stripped — prose describing the trap is not an implementation of it, nor evidence against one."* A naive grep for `SIGTERM` absence would fire on every CLI tool and every app with no capture tap. Arm 3's own stated approximation: *"Arm 3 compares offsets rather than parsing scopes, and deliberately only looks at the first `.resume()` that follows the file's first `makeSignalSource(`"* — an unrelated earlier `resume()` (URLSession, dispatch queue) is out of scope by construction.

**Minimal declarative capability.** Arms 1–2 are already expressible: `relevantWhen.repoContains` ×2 plus `repoWide.unlessSomeFileMatches` (both exist in `pattern-rules.mjs`). Arm 2's "token appears in no file in the set" is a repo-wide absence quantifier — also existing shape. Arm 3 needs one new primitive: **ordered-occurrence within a file** — "pattern A must occur before pattern B, where B's search begins at the first occurrence of C". Pattern-shaped, offset arithmetic only; no resolution or graph.

---

# 6. `gha/secrets-in-job-if`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/github-actions/secrets-in-job-if.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** `workflowFiles(ctx)` = `ctx.tracked` matching `/^\.github\/workflows\/[^/]+\.ya?ml$/` (`/home/user/Claudinite/engine/checks/helpers/github-workflows.mjs`).

**Parsing.** A **YAML indentation state machine over raw lines** — no `parseYaml`. Single forward pass carrying `stepsIndent`:
```js
const steps = /^(\s*)steps:\s*$/.exec(line);
if (steps) { stepsIndent = steps[1].length; return; }
if (/^\s{0,2}\S/.test(line)) stepsIndent = -1;   // new job or top-level key
const m = /^(\s*)if:\s*(.*)$/.exec(line);
if (m && /secrets\./.test(m[2]) && (stepsIndent === -1 || m[1].length <= stepsIndent)) { … }
```
i.e. an `if:` at or above the enclosing `steps:` indent is job-level; below it is step-level. `^\s{0,2}\S` resets the scope on any line indented ≤2.

**Asserts.** No job-level `if:` reads `secrets.*`.

**Naive-regex FP.** No banner. The FP a bare `/if:.*secrets\./` produces is precisely **step-level `if:`**, where reading `secrets.*` is legal and common — that is the entire content of the rule's scoping logic. Secondary FP: `if:` inside a `run:` block scalar or a composite-action-shaped file.

**Minimal declarative capability.** Exactly the capability you named: **a YAML-block-scoped line match — "lines within (or outside) the indented block opened by a line matching X"**, with the block closed by a dedent to a declared column. Here the assertion is the *complement* ("lines NOT inside the `steps:` block"), so the primitive needs both polarities. Nothing computational. A structural alternative (`jobs.<id>.if` via a real parser) is blocked by minimal-yaml's limits — see §11.

---

# 7. `gha/run-pipefail`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/github-actions/run-pipefail.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** Same `workflowFiles(ctx)`. File-level abstain: `if (text === null || /shell:\s*bash/.test(text)) continue;` — one `shell: bash` anywhere silences the file.

**Parsing.** A **YAML block-scalar body collector by indent**:
- `inline = /^(\s*)(?:-\s+)?run:\s*(.+)$/.exec(lines[i])`, `runIndent = inline[1].length`.
- If `inline[2]` matches `/^[|>][+-]?\s*$/` (a block-scalar introducer, chomping indicators included), the body is the following lines until a non-blank line whose first non-space column is `<= runIndent`.
- Otherwise the "body" is the single inline command.
- Pipe detection: `PIPE = /(^|[^|])\|([^|]|$)/` — commented in source as *"A single | between non-| characters is a shell pipe; || is the or-operator."*

**Asserts.** No `run:` step (inline or block-scalar) contains a shell pipe in a workflow that never sets `shell: bash`.

**Naive-regex FP.** No banner. A naive `/\|/` line grep flags: the `||` or-operator, the `run: |` introducer itself, YAML flow syntax, and any `|` in `name:`/`with:`/comments. Residual FPs the rule keeps: a `|` inside a quoted shell string (`echo "a|b"`) and a `|` inside a `#` comment line within the block scalar. Minor dead code: the `!/^\s+/` break at line 27 is subsumed by the `search(/\S/) <= runIndent` break on the next line, and the trailing `if (!lines[j].trim()) continue;` after the push is unreachable-effect.

**Minimal declarative capability.** The **same indented-block scope primitive as rule 6**, in its positive polarity plus a *block-scalar* opener: "the continuation lines of a line matching `/run:\s*[|>]/`, ending at dedent to the opener's column" — then an ordinary `matchLines` inside that scope, with the existing file-level `unlessFileMatches` for the `shell: bash` gate. Fully declarative once the block primitive exists.

---

# 8. `aws-sam/handler-path`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/aws-sam/handler-path.mjs` (blocking)

**Inputs / selection.** `samResources(ctx)` (`/home/user/Claudinite/engine/checks/helpers/sam-templates.mjs`) — every `ctx.tracked` path matching `/(^|\/)template\.ya?ml$/`, `parseYaml`ed, yielding `{templatePath, name, resource}` for each entry of `doc.Resources`.

**Parsing.** The only rule of the ten that uses a real document parser: `parseYaml` from `minimal-yaml.mjs`. All logic thereafter is field navigation on plain JS objects — `resource.Type`, `Metadata.BuildMethod`, `Metadata.BuildProperties.EntryPoints` / `.OutBase`, `Properties.Handler` — plus `entry.lastIndexOf('/')` for the subdir.

**Asserts.** For `AWS::Serverless::Function` with `BuildMethod: esbuild`, exactly one `EntryPoints` entry, no `OutBase`, and an entry containing `/`: `Properties.Handler` must not start with `<entryDir>/`.

**Naive-regex FP.** No banner; the equivalent is the *FP guards* comment — *"FP guards (from adversarial mining): skip when OutBase is set (it changes the drop) or when there is more than one entry point (behavior differs)."* A line grep for `Handler: src/...` would flag every non-esbuild function, every multi-entry build, and every `OutBase`-set build.

**Note.** The finding carries `file` but **no `line`** — a direct consequence of `parseYaml` discarding all source positions (§11).

**Minimal declarative capability.** Almost entirely covered by the existing `checkParsedFiles` family (`filesMatching`, `forEachEntryAtField: "Resources"`, `whereEntryFieldEquals: {field: "Type", equals: …}`, `whenFieldPresent`, `requireField`/`forbidField`). What is missing is **a cross-field relational assertion with a derived value**: "field `Properties.Handler` must not start with `dirname(Metadata.BuildProperties.EntryPoints[0])`", plus **array-cardinality gating** (`EntryPoints.length === 1`). That is a field-to-field comparison with one string transform — declarative-expressible, not computational.

---

# 9. `conformance-workflow`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/core/conformance-workflow.mjs` (**advisory**, deliberately — the header explains the promotion path)

**Inputs / selection.** Relevance gate first: `ctx.files.includes('.claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs')`, else `[]` (inert on non-members). Then all `ctx.files` under `.github/workflows/` matching `/\.ya?ml$/` — note `ctx.files`, not `ctx.tracked`, unlike the two GHA rules.

**Parsing.** Two nested hand-rolled **YAML block extractions**, both exported (so testable):
- `onBlock(text)` — from `text.search(/^on:/m)` to the first following line matching `/^[A-Za-z_-]+:/` (next top-level key). Header: *"Trigger filters (`paths:`) are nested INSIDE it, so scanning the whole file would confuse a job-level key with a trigger-level one."*
- `gatesEveryPull(text)` — within `onBlock`'s text, finds `/^\s+pull_request:/`, takes its indent, collects following lines until a non-blank line at `<= indent`, then tests `/^\s*paths(-ignore)?:/m` on that sub-block. `sweeps` is a plain whole-file `text.includes('engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs')`.

**Asserts.** File-set-level, three-way: if any workflow has `pull_request` + sweeps + **no** path filter → `return []` (a real gate exists). Else if some workflows sweep behind a filter → flag the first. Else if the repo has any `pull_request` workflow at all → flag "none of them runs the world sweep". A repo with no `pull_request` workflow at all is deliberately not flagged (#588: the delivery merges directly).

**Naive-regex FP.** No banner; the equivalent is the three-shape table in the header (*"a PATH-FILTERED flow → the arm succeeds, and no check ever runs. The PR waits forever. THIS is the trap."*). A naive `grep paths:` would hit job-level and step-level `paths:` keys, and `grep pull_request` cannot distinguish a filtered trigger from an unfiltered one.

**Minimal declarative capability.** Two layers: (a) the **nested YAML block scope** of rules 6/7, applied twice (`on:` → `pull_request:`), and (b) a **repo-wide "unless some file satisfies a conjunction" quantifier**. Layer (b) already exists as `repoWide.unlessSomeFileMatches` + `flagFilesMatching` groups, but today it can only test whole-file regexes — it cannot ask "matches `pull_request:` *within the `on:` block* AND contains SWEEP AND does *not* match `paths:` *within the `pull_request:` block*". So the missing piece is purely feeding a block-scoped view into the existing quantifier. Nothing computational. Line 96 re-reads every workflow with a whole-file `/^\s+pull_request:/m` — an unscoped shortcut that would inherit the same view.

---

# 10. `python-optional-import-top-level`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/python/skills/python-optional-deps/optional-import-lazy.mjs` (blocking)
**Shared helper** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/python/skills/python-optional-deps/pyproject.mjs`

**Inputs / selection.** Gate: every `ctx.files` path matching `/(^|\/)pyproject\.toml$/` (excluding `skills/python-optional-deps/`) → `optionalDistNames()`; if the union is empty, `return []`. Judged set: `ctx.files` matching `/\.py$/`, minus the skill's own dir, minus `TESTISH = /(^|\/)(tests?|__tests__)\/|(^|\/)(test_[^/]*|conftest)\.py$|_test\.py$/`.

**Parsing.** Three layers, all line-based:
- **TOML section scan** (`optionalDistNames`, explicitly *"Line-based (the engine carries no TOML parser)"*): track `/^\s*\[([^\]]+)\]/` headers, set `inSection = header === 'project.optional-dependencies'`, and inside it treat every quoted token as a requirement, taking its leading `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/` name, lowercased. The rarer inline `optional-dependencies = { … }` form is not parsed — a declared safe false-negative.
- **Dist→import name mapping** (`importNamesFor`): the name itself plus `[-.] → _`. Names whose import differs unrelatedly (Pillow→PIL, opencv-python→cv2, PyYAML→yaml) are deliberately unmapped, so unflagged.
- **Python top-level import classification**: `TOP_LEVEL_IMPORT = /^(import|from)\s/` — **column 0 is the whole "module top level" test** (outside any `def`/`class`/`try` by construction) — then `topPackagesOf(line.split('#')[0])` (`from a.b import c` → `a`; relative `from . import x` → `[]`; `import a.b as x, c` → `a, c`).

**Asserts.** No column-0 import in a non-test `.py` file names a package the repo itself declared optional.

**Naive-regex FP.** Banner is `RELEVANCE FIRST` rather than `PARSED, NOT GREPPED`; the key sentence: *"a skill check runs on EVERY repo, so the gate is what makes the signal false-positive-free — the repo must declare optional dependencies in a pyproject.toml ([project.optional-dependencies] is the ONLY place a package is DECLARED optional), and only those exact packages are in scope."* A naive `^import tensorflow` grep flags every project that legitimately hard-depends on it. The try/except-guarded import is excluded *mechanically* (indented ⇒ never column 0), not by a special case.

**Minimal declarative capability.** This is the one that breaks the pattern model most cleanly: **the matched token set is derived from another file's contents**. The primitive needed is a *data-derived pattern* — "extract a token set from file X under a scoped region (TOML section / JSON field), normalize it, then match lines in file set Y against a pattern template parameterized by that set". Everything else (column-0 anchoring, test-file exclusion) is existing vocabulary. Not a graph walk; a single cross-file value join, bounded and non-recursive.

---

# 11. `python-optional-import-install-hint`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/packs/python/skills/python-optional-deps/optional-import-install-hint.mjs` (**advisory** — *"whether a message names the exact extra is a wording judgment, so this nudges rather than blocks"*)

**Inputs / selection.** Identical gate and file set to rule 10 (same `optionalImportNames(ctx)`, same `SELF`/`TESTISH`/`PY_EXT` filters).

**Parsing.** A genuine **Python indentation-block parser** — `offendingGuards(text, importNames)`:
- Find `mtry = /^(\s*)try\s*:/`; `base = mtry[1].length`.
- **try-body scope**: lines with `indentOf(line) > base`, blanks skipped, until the first dedent to `<= base`; within it, `isImport(code) && topPackagesOf(code).some(p => importNames.has(p))` sets `importsOptional`.
- **Clause check**: the dedent line must be at *exactly* `base` and match `/^\s*except\b.*\bImportError\b/`, else abstain.
- **except-body scope**: same indent rule; records the first `/^\s*raise\b/` line and whether any line contains `/\bpip install\b/`.
- Fires only when `raiseLine !== null && !hasHint`.

**Asserts.** A `try/except ImportError` guard whose *own try-body* imports a declared-optional package, and whose except-body re-raises, carries a `pip install` hint in that except-body.

**Naive-regex FP.** Header: *"a block is only in scope when ITS OWN try-body imports one of those exact packages (so an unrelated `except ImportError` — a fallback import, a feature probe — is never touched)."* Declared out of scope, never an FP: the availability-probe shape `except ImportError: HAVE_TF = False` has no `raise`, so it never fires; that residue stays prose in the python pack's RULES.md.

**Minimal declarative capability.** The **indentation-block scope primitive generalized**: "a block opened by a line matching X at column C, body = deeper-indented lines to dedent, optionally followed by a *clause* line at exactly column C matching Y with its own body", plus within-scope `require`/`forbid` assertions and a *co-occurrence* condition across two sibling scopes (try-body imports ⇒ except-body must contain hint). This is the *same* primitive rules 6, 7 and 9 need, with a "sibling clause" extension — YAML indent blocks and Python indent blocks are one shape. Plus the same data-derived token set as rule 10. Nothing computational.

---

# 12. `pack-discovery-entry-await`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/pack-discovery-entry-await.mjs` (blocking, repo-local pack)

| input shape | result |
|---|---|
| `a: 1` / `b: \|` + body / `c: 3` (map context) | `{"a":1,"b":"\|"}` — **`c` silently dropped**; a block scalar in a plain map truncates every following sibling key |

# Helper: `engine/checks/helpers/minimal-yaml.mjs`

**File** `/home/user/Claudinite/engine/checks/helpers/minimal-yaml.mjs` (117 lines)

**Header, verbatim scope statement:** *"A MINIMAL YAML-subset parser — dependency-free, sufficient to query the STRUCTURE of SAM/CloudFormation templates (nested block maps, block and flow sequences, scalars). Deliberately NOT a general YAML parser: no anchors/aliases, no multi-line block scalars (`|` `>`), no flow maps; CloudFormation short tags (!Ref, !Sub, !GetAtt …) keep their scalar value, the tag is dropped; it never throws… Good enough for the SAM/CloudFormation template checks; do not use it for arbitrary YAML."*

**Exported API:** `parseYaml(text)` only. Everything else (`stripComment`, `scalar`, `flowSeq`, `parseBlock`, `splitKey`) is module-private.

**Structure preserved.**
- Nested maps: **yes** — `parseBlock` recurses on indent increase, keyed by `splitKey` (first unquoted `:` followed by space or EOL, quoted keys unwrapped).
- Sequences: **yes** — block sequences including the `- key: value` map-item form (deeper lines gathered into a synthetic sub-block), and flow sequences `[a, b]` via `flowSeq`.
- Line numbers / source positions: **no.** `parseYaml` returns plain JS values with no provenance whatsoever. Blank lines and comment-only lines are dropped before parsing, so even index reconstruction is impossible. This is directly visible in rule 8: `aws-sam/handler-path`'s `finding()` carries `file` but no `line`, while all nine line-based rules carry one.

**Empirically verified failure modes** (run against the helper directly):

| input shape | result |
|---|---|
| `a: 1` / `b: \|` + body / `c: 3` (map context) | `{"a":1,"b":"\|"}` — **`c` silently dropped**; a block scalar in a plain map truncates every following sibling key |
| `- run: \|` + body + `name: n` (sequence item) | `[{"run":"\|"}]` — body lost, **and the step's own sibling key `name` lost**; the sequence branch recovers the outer index but the item's map is truncated |
| `push: {branches: [main]}` | `{"push":"{branches: [main]}"}` — flow map returned as a raw string |
| `a: &x 1` / `b: *x` | `{"a":"&x 1","b":"*x"}` — anchors/aliases returned as junk strings |
| a realistic workflow with `on:`/`jobs:`/`steps:` | `on` survives as the literal string key `'on'` (better than spec-YAML, which would coerce it to boolean `true`); `jobs.<id>.steps` is a proper array of maps |

**Verdict on per-step assertions inside workflow jobs.** The *shape* is there — `jobs` is a nested map, `steps` is a sequence of maps, so `jobs.<id>.steps[n].if` is addressable in principle. In practice it does **not** support per-step assertions, for two independent reasons:

1. **Block scalars destroy the step.** `run: |` is the dominant form in real workflows, and it both loses the command body and drops every sibling key declared *after* it in the same step map (and, in a plain-map context, every sibling key in the enclosing block). Neither `gha/run-pipefail` (needs the body) nor `gha/secrets-in-job-if` (needs a reliable `if` alongside `run`) could be ported onto it as written — which is exactly why both are line-based.
2. **No line provenance.** Findings on parsed structure can only anchor at the file. The two GHA rules both anchor at a line, and a step-level finding without a line is materially worse.

To carry per-step workflow assertions, `minimal-yaml` would need (a) block-scalar support (`|`, `>`, with chomping/indentation indicators) and (b) source-line provenance on every node — e.g. each map/sequence node carrying the 1-based line of its key, or a parallel path→line index.

---

# Helper survey: scoped/indented-block scanning

**Grepped** `engine/checks/helpers/` for `indent|block|scope` (case-insensitive), plus `indentedBlock|blockAt|scopeOf|withinBlock`.

**No such helper exists.** `indent` appears only inside `minimal-yaml.mjs`'s own private `parseBlock`. `block` elsewhere means markdown fenced-code blanking (`pattern-rules.mjs` line 461: *"Fenced code blocks blanked line-for-line, so line numbers never shift"*) or markdown **bullet blocks** (`pattern-rules.mjs` lines 182–183: *"a bullet BLOCK is the bullet plus its indented continuation lines"*, driving `eachBulletBlockMatches` / `maxBulletBlockLength`). `scope` elsewhere means `reference-scanning.mjs`'s `scope: "imports"` edge qualifier and `work.mjs`'s `rule.scope === 'work'` context selector — neither is textual.

The markdown bullet-block logic in `pattern-rules.mjs` (≈ lines 545–555) is the closest existing thing: it *is* an indented-continuation-block gatherer, but it is hard-wired to column-0 markdown bullets and only concatenates the block for whole-block regex/length assertions — it exposes no general "open a scope at a line matching X, close it at dedent" primitive.

**Consequence.** Four rules each reimplement the same primitive from scratch, with slightly different conventions:

| rule | opener | close condition | polarity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gha/secrets-in-job-if` | `/^(\s*)steps:\s*$/` | any line matching `/^\s{0,2}\S/` | flag lines **outside** / at-or-above |
| `gha/run-pipefail` | `/^(\s*)(?:-\s+)?run:\s*[\|>][+-]?$/` | non-blank line with `search(/\S/) <= runIndent` | flag lines **inside** |
| `conformance-workflow` | `/^on:/m`, then `/^\s+pull_request:/` | next `/^[A-Za-z_-]+:/`; then non-blank at `<= indent` | test pattern **inside** (nested twice) |
| `optional-import-install-hint` | `/^(\s*)try\s*:/` | `indentOf(line) <= base`; sibling clause at `=== base` | require/forbid **inside**, two sibling bodies |

---

# Cross-cutting judgment

**One primitive would carry five of the ten rules.** A `blockScope` declarative key — *"the lines of the indented block opened by a line matching X at its own column, closed at the first non-blank dedent, optionally with a sibling clause line at exactly that column matching Y and its own body; assertions apply inside (or, with inverted polarity, outside) that scope"* — would express `gha/secrets-in-job-if`, `gha/run-pipefail`, `conformance-workflow` (nested), and the block half of `python-optional-import-install-hint`, and would let `pattern-rules.mjs`'s existing `repoWide` quantifier serve rule 9 unchanged. It is line-and-column arithmetic, nothing more.

**A second primitive carries three more.** A `bracketScope` — *"for each match of X ending at an opening bracket, the balanced region to its match, string/template-aware; assert over its own top-level keys or its raw text; abstain when unbalanced or when the region is not a literal"* — covers `declarative-content-set-icon`, `leaflet/tile-attribution`, and the entry-block half of `pack-discovery-entry-await`. Plus a `tagScope` variant with attribute binding for `leaflet/asset-integrity`.

**Supporting source views, all offset-preserving, all pattern-shaped:** comments-blanked (exists as `scanIgnoringComments`), string-literals-blanked (new — needed by rules 1 and 12), HTML-comments-blanked, and "the JS an HTML page actually runs, spliced back at original offsets" (rule 4's `codeView`).

**Genuinely non-pattern, in ascending order of cost:**
1. **Ordered occurrence** (`signal-teardown-routing` arm 3): pattern A before pattern B, B's search seeded at C. Offset comparison — trivially addable.
2. **Cross-field relational assertion with a derived value** (`aws-sam/handler-path`): `Handler` must not start with `dirname(EntryPoints[0])`, gated on array cardinality. One string transform over already-parsed fields.
3. **Data-derived pattern / cross-file value join** (both python rules): the token set being matched is extracted from a *different* file's scoped region (TOML section) and normalized. Bounded, non-recursive, but a real departure from static patterns.
4. **Parsed-field → scan-scope join** (`content-script-module-syntax`): the *file set* being scanned is computed from a JSON field, path-resolved against the declaring file's directory.
5. **Transitive import-closure selection** (`pack-discovery-entry-await`): a fixpoint over a resolved module graph. **This is the only rule that is irreducibly computational** — the others are pattern-shaped once given the right scope and view. `module-imports.mjs` already ships `relativeImports` + `resolveRelative`, so the engine work is a selector wrapper, not new algorithms.</result>

# Commitlint Rules Configuration

## Tuple Structure

Commitlint rules follow a three-element configuration array: **"Rules are made up by a name and a configuration array. The configuration array contains: Level [0..2], Applicable always|never, Value."**

The components are:

1. **Level** (0-2): Controls enforcement severity—0 disables, 1 warns, 2 errors
2. **Applicable** (always|never): Determines if the rule applies normally or inverted
3. **Value**: The specific parameter for that rule

## Configuration Formats

Rules support three implementation patterns:

- **Plain arrays**: Direct configuration values
- **Functions**: Dynamic rules returning arrays
- **Async functions**: Asynchronous rule resolution

The documentation states: **"Rule configurations are either of type array residing on a key with the rule's name as key on the rules object or of type function returning type array or Promise<array>."**

This design allows both static and dynamic rule configurations, enabling commitlint to handle complex validation scenarios beyond simple hardcoded values.

# Conftest: Supported Formats and Architecture

## Supported File Formats

Conftest can parse and test policies against these formats:

- CUE
- CycloneDX
- Dockerfile
- EDN
- Environment files (.env)
- HCL and HCL2
- HOCON
- Ignore files (.gitignore, .dockerignore)
- INI
- JSON
- Jsonnet
- nginx
- Property files (.properties)
- SPDX
- TextProto (Protocol Buffers)
- TOML
- VCL
- XML
- YAML

## Architecture

**Policy Language:** Conftest uses the Rego language from Open Policy Agent. As the documentation states: *"Conftest relies on the Rego language from Open Policy Agent for writing policies."*

**Parsing Process:** Configuration files are parsed into structured data that Rego policies can evaluate. The tool *"looks for `deny`, `violation`, and `warn` rules"* within these policies to assess compliance.

**Workflow:** Users write test policies in Rego files (conventionally in a `policy` directory), and Conftest evaluates structured configuration data against these rules, producing pass/fail results based on policy violations detected.

**Header, verbatim scope statement:** *"A MINIMAL YAML-subset parser — dependency-free, sufficient to query the STRUCTURE of SAM/CloudFormation templates (nested block maps, block and flow sequences, scalars). **Exported API:** `parseYaml(text)` only. Everything else (`stripComment`, `scalar`, `flowSeq`, `parseBlock`, `splitKey`) is module-private.

**Structure preserved.**
- Nested maps: **yes** — `parseBlock` recurses on indent increase, keyed by `splitKey` (first unquoted `:` followed by space or EOL, quoted keys unwrapped).
- Sequences: **yes** — block sequences including the `- key: value` map-item form (deeper lines gathered into a synthetic sub-block), and flow sequences `[a, b]` via `flowSeq`.
- Line numbers / source positions: **no.** `parseYaml` returns plain JS values with no provenance whatsoever. Blank lines and comment-only lines are dropped before parsing, so even index reconstruction is impossible. This is directly visible in rule 8: `aws-sam/handler-path`'s `finding()` carries `file` but no `line`, while all nine line-based rules carry one.

**Empirically verified failure modes** (run against the helper directly):

| input shape | result |
|---|---|
| `a: 1` / `b: \|` + body / `c: 3` (map context) | `{"a":1,"b":"\|"}` — **`c` silently dropped**; a block scalar in a plain map truncates every following sibling key |
| `- run: \|` + body + `name: n` (sequence item) | `[{"run":"\|"}]` — body lost, **and the step's own sibling key `name` lost**; the sequence branch recovers the outer index but the item's map is truncated |
| `push: {branches: [main]}` | `{"push":"{branches: [main]}"}` — flow map returned as a raw string |
| `a: &x 1` / `b: *x` | `{"a":"&x 1","b":"*x"}` — anchors/aliases returned as junk strings |
| a realistic workflow with `on:`/`jobs:`/`steps:` | `on` survives as the literal string key `'on'` (better than spec-YAML, which would coerce it to boolean `true`); `jobs.<id>.steps` is a proper array of maps |

**Verdict on per-step assertions inside workflow jobs.** The *shape* is there — `jobs` is a nested map, `steps` is a sequence of maps, so `jobs.<id>.steps[n].if` is addressable in principle. In practice it does **not** support per-step assertions, for two independent reasons:

1. **Block scalars destroy the step.** `run: |` is the dominant form in real workflows, and it both loses the command body and drops every sibling key declared *after* it in the same step map (and, in a plain-map context, every sibling key in the enclosing block). Neither `gha/run-pipefail` (needs the body) nor `gha/secrets-in-job-if` (needs a reliable `if` alongside `run`) could be ported onto it as written — which is exactly why both are line-based.
2. **No line provenance.** Findings on parsed structure can only anchor at the file. The two GHA rules both anchor at a line, and a step-level finding without a line is materially worse.

To carry per-step workflow assertions, `minimal-yaml` would need (a) block-scalar support (`|`, `>`, with chomping/indentation indicators) and (b) source-line provenance on every node — e.g. each map/sequence node carrying the 1-based line of its key, or a parallel path→line index.

# Cross-cutting judgment

**One primitive would carry five of the ten rules.** A `blockScope` declarative key — *"the lines of the indented block opened by a line matching X at its own column, closed at the first non-blank dedent, optionally with a sibling clause line at exactly that column matching Y and its own body; assertions apply inside (or, with inverted polarity, outside) that scope"* — would express `gha/secrets-in-job-if`, `gha/run-pipefail`, `conformance-workflow` (nested), and the block half of `python-optional-import-install-hint`, and would let `pattern-rules.mjs`'s existing `repoWide` quantifier serve rule 9 unchanged. It is line-and-column arithmetic, nothing more.

**A second primitive carries three more.** A `bracketScope` — *"for each match of X ending at an opening bracket, the balanced region to its match, string/template-aware; assert over its own top-level keys or its raw text; abstain when unbalanced or when the region is not a literal"* — covers `declarative-content-set-icon`, `leaflet/tile-attribution`, and the entry-block half of `pack-discovery-entry-await`. Plus a `tagScope` variant with attribute binding for `leaflet/asset-integrity`.

**Supporting source views, all offset-preserving, all pattern-shaped:** comments-blanked (exists as `scanIgnoringComments`), string-literals-blanked (new — needed by rules 1 and 12), HTML-comments-blanked, and "the JS an HTML page actually runs, spliced back at original offsets" (rule 4's `codeView`).

**Genuinely non-pattern, in ascending order of cost:**
1. **Ordered occurrence** (`signal-teardown-routing` arm 3): pattern A before pattern B, B's search seeded at C. Offset comparison — trivially addable.
2. **Cross-field relational assertion with a derived value** (`aws-sam/handler-path`): `Handler` must not start with `dirname(EntryPoints[0])`, gated on array cardinality. One string transform over already-parsed fields.
3. **Data-derived pattern / cross-file value join** (both python rules): the token set being matched is extracted from a *different* file's scoped region (TOML section) and normalized. Bounded, non-recursive, but a real departure from static patterns.
4. **Parsed-field → scan-scope join** (`content-script-module-syntax`): the *file set* being scanned is computed from a JSON field, path-resolved against the declaring file's directory.
5. **Transitive import-closure selection** (`pack-discovery-entry-await`): a fixpoint over a resolved module graph. **This is the only rule that is irreducibly computational** — the others are pattern-shaped once given the right scope and view. `module-imports.mjs` already ships `relativeImports` + `resolveRelative`, so the engine work is a selector wrapper, not new algorithms.</result>

input.body:
Comment class: other
(review of this inventory, dispatched 2026-08-15; the deliverable is the conversion method below plus PR #891, which lands the class-A slice)

Every class-A module was re-read against the engine, and the three survey classes (B/C/D/E) were re-derived rule by rule from the sources. The inventory's classification is sound; its **key proposals and its ceiling are not**. The honest backlog is not 7 — with the discipline "enhance an existing option before minting a field," it is **10 of the 54 through `declared-checks.json`, plus ~3 more through a second declarative surface**, and the remainder stays coded for reasons worth naming precisely.

## The method (the actual answer to "suggest a way")

1. **Enhance a seam that already exists** — a new quantifier or coverage form on `requireIndexCoverage`, a view flag on an existing probe, a relational refinement on a `matchLines` entry. Same move `unlessPreviousLineMatches` already made.
2. **A new scanning primitive ships only as sub-keys of an existing assertion family, with ≥2 customers named** (the #707 test), never as a new family.
3. **New surfaces arrive as formats or manifest seams, not keys** — a TOML parser behind the existing parse cache; a `configSchema` on pack manifests.
4. Every conversion **red-first against the coded rule's own fixtures, module deleted in the same commit** (the #839 pattern; all of #891 followed it).

## Corrections to this inventory (applied in #891)

- **`andPreviousLineMatches` is unnecessary.** `checkEachFile.forbid` is a whole-text regex: one pattern covers the plist same-line, next-line, *and* comment-interleaved layouts — more than a line-pair key would. The macOS rule converted with zero new match keys; what it actually needed, and the inventory missed, was `ignoringComments` on `someTrackedFileContains` (the fixture "a comment naming the teardown must not arm the rule" fails on the raw-text probe).
- **`requireValueInArray` is not "the exact mirror".** The declarative form reads the RAW `packs` array — the coded rules read the *normalized* config — so the membership test must count `{ "id": "core" }` by its field, or the existing object-entry fixtures go red. Landed as `matchingEntryObjectsByField` on both polarity twins.
- **The privacy and home-seeded rules are one enhancement, not two keys**: both are `requireIndexCoverage` with a new quantifier (`eachValueInParsedArray` / `whoseTextMatches`) or coverage form (`coveredByValueInArrayAtField`).
- **The tally claim is wrong**: `packRules` already counts declared checks (that's what `catalog-tally.test.mjs` derives — 91 pre-branch includes the 37), so conversions are tally-neutral; only the product-wiki *split* moved it, 91→92.
- The #838 housekeeping note checks out: `unlessPreviousLineMatches`/`maxLineLength`/`andLineMatches` are all landed and used — that bullet can be ticked.

## The next two tranches (not in #891, sized and named)

**Indented-block relations on `matchLines`** — the survey's strongest fact: *four* coded rules hand-roll the same indent-scope walk with four slightly different close conventions (`gha/secrets-in-job-if`, `gha/run-pipefail`, `conformance-workflow`, `python-optional-import-install-hint`), and the engine has a fifth hard-wired copy in the markdown bullet-block gatherer. The field settled this shape long ago: Semgrep's `pattern-inside`/`pattern-not-inside`, ast-grep's relational `inside`/`has` with `stopBy` (both re-verified against current docs today). As matchLines sub-keys — a has-direction `unlessIndentedBlockBelowMatches`, an inside-direction `whenWithinBlockOpenedBy`/`unlessWithinBlockOpenedBy`, block = opener line's column to first non-blank dedent, `|`/`>` block scalars included — it converts `gha/checkout-submodules`, `gha/secrets-in-job-if`, and `gha/run-pipefail` outright. `conformance-workflow` still doesn't convert (its verdict is a three-way decision over the file *set*, beyond `repoWide` even with block views), and the python pair additionally needs TOML + data-derived token sets — both stay coded until those exist.

**A third `scanFiles` form: files named by a parsed field.** `scanFiles` already accepts two shapes (regex | exact path); an object form — field path, resolved against the naming file's directory, silently dropped when the target is outside the scan set — converts `web-speech-no-window-api-in-service-worker` faithfully and `firebase/functions-node-pin` (with a declared default + suffix), and is the primary arm of `content-script-module-syntax`. Prior art: Spectral's `given`+`resolved` (select through references), Conftest's parse-everything-into-one-document-model architecture (19 formats, one query surface).

**The config cluster converts through the manifest, not declared-checks**: a `configSchema` seam on `pack.mjs` (ESLint's `meta.schema` idiom, already recommended by `docs/declarative-checks/REVIEW.md` §4) retires `growth-config` and kin as hand-rolled validators. That's ~3 more rules off the coded list via a *different* declarative surface — worth its own issue.

**Deferred with named triggers, not refused**: a work-scope vocabulary (commit-message assertions — commitlint's `rules:` config is exactly this as data; one customer today, trigger = a second consumer pack wanting commit conventions); TOML as a parsed format (trigger = the python pair once block-clauses exist); an `importClosureOf` file selector (`module-imports.mjs` already ships the machinery; one customer, and it's the only genuinely computational *selection* in the corpus).

## Where this inventory was right, sharpened

Class E stays coded, and the survey hardened the argument: an export-reference key (`patternFromExport`) would be the declaration format's **first dynamic import**, against the "a declaration states its own case" rule the format enforces — and in every E rule, real logic survives beyond the referenced value (task-declaration-shape's cross-field conditionals, version-scheme's config-derived n-way equality, the preferences store's composite predicate). Transcript and base-vs-head rules likewise; the three JSON-diff rules want `work.addedKeys` (#838) and become *shorter coded rules*. Genuinely computational and staying so: `file-placement`'s distance metric, `markdown-link-labels`' normalize-and-compare, `pack-discovery-entry-await`'s graph walk.

Sources beyond this tree: ast-grep relational-rule and Semgrep rule-syntax docs, conftest.dev, commitlint rules reference (all read 2026-08-15), on top of REVIEW.md's 2026-08-14 survey.

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.

It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
